context: Normalize one level of outer plain parentheses in normalize_columns (mirror the existing tuple( handling: strip a single balanced outer '(...)' wrapper before splitting), with an explicit collision review in the PR description: confirm the change cannot make two DIFFERENT key expressions compare equal (the comma-split tokenization is applied identically to both sides, and the probe f(a),b vs f(a,b) still tokenizes differently). Add live chDB coverage for the multi-column shape end-to-end (ledger record -> introspect -> corroborate -> corroborated=True). Document the expression-canonicalization limitation in the receipts design note and pin toYYYYMM verbatim survival with a live assertion.
description:
From the 2026-07-31 adversarial review, proven against live chDB.

Defect (R2, fail-closed but silent and generator-reachable): for CREATE TABLE ... PARTITION BY (a, b), system.tables.partition_key comes back as the string '(a, b)' - WITH parentheses. normalize_columns (benchbox/core/tuning/introspection.py:284-305) strips '[...]' and 'tuple(...)' wrappers but not plain parens, so the expected ('a','b') mismatches the observed ('(a','b)') forever: a multi-column-partition tuned run can NEVER reach applied_verified, with no error anywhere. The shipped generator emits exactly this shape for two partitioning columns (benchbox/core/tuning/generators/clickhouse.py:211 joins 'a, b'; clickhouse/workload.py:154 renders 'PARTITION BY (a, b)'). The existing live tests (tests/integration/test_clickhouse_applied_ledger_live.py) only cover single-expression partitions, which is why this survived - it is exactly the invisible fail-closed class that file's docstring warns about.

Related, same family (document, do not over-fix): ClickHouse canonicalizes expression sugar in the catalog - ORDER BY (toStartOfInterval(t, INTERVAL 1 DAY)) is stored as toStartOfInterval(t, toIntervalDay(1)) -> permanent mismatch for any sugar form. toYYYYMM survives verbatim (verified live), so the shipped generator is safe today; the limitation must be documented and pinned by a live test so a future generator change cannot silently regress into never-verifying.

anti_patterns.dont: Do not attempt to canonicalize ClickHouse expression sugar (INTERVAL 1 DAY -> toIntervalDay(1)) in BenchBox
anti_patterns.instead: document the limitation as known fail-closed behavior and pin it with a live test
anti_patterns.why: reimplementing ClickHouse's expression canonicalizer is unbounded and version-dependent

anti_patterns.dont: Do not fix by making the ClickHouse introspector rewrite catalog strings platform-specifically
anti_patterns.instead: fix normalize_columns once, cover with unit vectors from all three shipped introspectors
anti_patterns.why: the same normalize_columns is the shared comparison contract for every platform; a platform-side rewrite hides the shared-contract gap

anti_patterns.dont: Do not strip ALL parentheses from catalog or intent text
anti_patterns.instead: strip exactly one balanced OUTER wrapper, then keep the existing tokenizer
anti_patterns.why: that would collapse different expressions (f(a),b vs f(a,b)) into equal tuples and could mint a false corroboration - the one direction this system must never fail

preserves.behavior: Fail-closed direction on any ambiguity: when in doubt, mismatch/unverifiable, never corroborated.
Matching stays order-sensitive exact tuple comparison - no substring or set-equality loosening.
No screen-scraping of SHOW CREATE TABLE; system.tables structured columns remain the only ClickHouse catalog source.
Single-expression partition keys (toYYYYMM(col)) keep corroborating verbatim (pinned by existing live tests).

verifications.command: uv run -- python -c "from benchbox.core.tuning.applied_ledger import PHASE_DDL, AppliedTuningLedger; from benchbox.core.tuning.introspection import corroborate; from benchbox.platforms.clickhouse.client import ClickHouseLocalClient; from benchbox.platforms.clickhouse.introspection import ClickHouseTuningIntrospector; c=ClickHouseLocalClient(); c.execute('DROP TABLE IF EXISTS zz_mc'); ddl='CREATE TABLE zz_mc (a Int32, b Int32, c Int32) ENGINE=MergeTree PARTITION BY (a, b) ORDER BY (c)'; c.execute(ddl); led=AppliedTuningLedger(); led.record(ddl, PHASE_DDL, table='zz_mc'); r=corroborate(led, ClickHouseTuningIntrospector().introspect(c, led)); assert r.corroborated, [e.to_dict() for e in r.entries]"
verifications.description: Multi-column partition corroborates against live chDB (post-fix probe)
verifications.expected: exit 0: both sort_key and partition_key intents corroborated against the real catalog

verifications.command: uv run -- python -c "from benchbox.core.tuning.introspection import normalize_columns as n; assert n('f(a), b') != n('f(a, b)'); assert n('(a, b)') == n('a, b') == n('tuple(a, b)')"
verifications.description: No false-equality collisions introduced by paren stripping
verifications.expected: exit 0: wrapper forms unify; distinct expressions stay distinct

Pytest was initially waiting on the legitimate shared lock, so the tracker ladder direct probes established red without bypassing it.

work_units.summary: Live chDB regression: multi-column PARTITION BY (a, b) must corroborate (fails today); unit vectors for '(a, b)', 'tuple(a, b)', '[a, b]', bare and single-expression forms

work_units.evidence: normalize_columns now removes exactly one balanced plain outer parenthesis wrapper before the existing tokenizer. Both exact post-fix live chDB and false-equality collision probes exit 0; malformed/unbalanced and nested wrapper tests remain fail-closed.
work_units.notes: normalize_columns: strip one balanced outer plain-paren wrapper (guarding against stripping a function call like 'f(a, b)' where the wrapper IS the argument list - only strip when the parens enclose the entire string and removing them leaves balanced text), with collision-analysis notes in the PR.

work_units.summary: Live-pin expression canonicalization: toYYYYMM corroborates verbatim, sugar forms honestly mismatch; document both
